LESSON: WRITING 1.5.1 WRITING LEGIBLY AND NEATLY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.5: Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should one write legibly and neatly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. classify letters according to height differentials
2. write a text, legibly and neatly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 1.5.1 WRITING LEGIBLY AND NEATLY
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 1.5.1 WRITING LEGIBLY AND NEATLY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Classify letters according to height differentials

What this means
In this part you learn to classify letters according to height differentials. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify letters according to height differentials.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify letters according to height differentials. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a text, legibly and neatly

What this means
In this part you learn to write a text, legibly and neatly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a text, legibly and neatly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a text, legibly and neatly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: classify letters according to height differentials)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly to a partner. (skill: write a text, legibly and neatly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: classify letters according to height differentials.
3. Practise this skill: write a text, legibly and neatly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should one write legibly and neatly?
2. What are the qualities of a good handwriting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: classify letters according to height differentials.
5. Be able to: write a text, legibly and neatly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
